findings.title: Model-deceit recommendations omit structured provenance
findings.what: The returned recommendation asserts contradicted/unbacked claim totals and a flagged-session count, but lines 72-83 include only display evidence and no provenance object identifying deceitSignals fields, source artifact, observed values, or inference. The five-row evidence cap also cannot independently reproduce larger totals.
findings.fix: Add structured provenance observations for flagged session count, unbackedClaimCount, and contradictedClaimCount with their deceitSignals source/field names and values, plus an inference describing the parser-derived classification.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with multiple flagged sessions produces a recommendation whose provenance validator passes and whose observations reproduce affected, contradicted, unbacked, and flagged-session totals from deceitSignals.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read src/lib/detectors/security/model-deceit.ts:21-83 and its batch test at lines 29-109. The tests confirm totals and capped display snippets but do not reveal any provenance property; the production return object ends at evidence.

findings.title: Model-latency recommendation lacks provenance and freshness demotion
findings.what: The detector recommends rerouting work and reports a reclaimed-time estimate from historical telemetry, but the returned object has no structured provenance for cohort rates, sample sizes, equal-output-volume arithmetic, or source fields. It also ignores sample timestamps, so arbitrarily old measurements remain phrased as current without an 'as of <date>' demotion.
findings.fix: Carry the latest contributing client_timestamp through candidate selection; add provenance observations for both cohorts and the reclaimed-time calculation, record asOf/stale, and demote stale detail/action wording.
findings.acceptance: Given dated slow and baseline cohorts, the recommendation passes provenance validation, exposes observations sufficient to recompute reclaimedMs, reports the latest contributing date, and uses explicitly historical 'as of <date>' wording once the freshness threshold is exceeded.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read src/lib/detectors/speed/model-latency.ts:89-137 and its batch test at lines 44-110. The return object contains evidence rows but no provenance/asOf fields, while the test fixtures carry client_timestamp and never assert freshness or provenance.
